page.layout: One block of text: a printed ornament at the top, then the title and heading centred, then the elegy in verse lines with a large woodcut initial N at the left; a catchword-like word "Antoni" set at the right foot of the text. No margin notes, no page number.

l.i: NOn frustra medium laudauì docta
vetustas:
Nam nil laudari dignius orbis
habet.
In medio posita est virtus: hinc indeque fallax
Tota sinistra via est, totaque dextra via
est, Icare, si patrem esses inter utrumque sequutus,
Icarias nullius nomine nosset aquas.
Si medio Phaëton mansisset calle superbus,
Non esset sava terra perusta face.
Nec lenis nimium, nec durat sæva potestas:
Quæ medium seruat, sola perennis erit.
Te nimia, o Iuli, clementia perdidit olim:
Sævitia occidit te, truculente Nero.
Augustus felix multos cur mansit in annos?
Nec facilis nimium, nec truculentus erat.
Vana superstitio non placat numinis iras,
Quod media gaudet simplicitate coli.
Largus opum nullus, nullus laudatus avarus:
Magnus in his potuit qui tenuisse modum.

page.notes: The large initial N is a woodcut ornament letter. Some words in the verse are set in italic with long s rendered as s; the letters u/v and i/j were normalised per the house rule. The line "Antoni" at the foot is a catchword. Several letters in the italic verse are faint and are transcribed as printed as far as legible.
